issues.item: Threat: Avoid Unfamiliar Places: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
issues.explanation: 'Avoid Unfamiliar Places' is an avoidance/safety behaviour rather than a threat appraisal item. In this profile, the Threat node otherwise contains felt current danger and reliving; this item is misclassified and weakens within-node coherence.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Authority Figures: Being around people in authority or uniform
issues.explanation: 'Avoid Authority Figures' is not phrased as a strategy and appears to describe a trigger category. It is also weakly supported by the rest of the profile, since no memory, threat, or appraisal content specifically involves authorities or uniforms. This creates a cross-node mismatch and a node-level inconsistency within Maladaptive Strategies.

vignette:
Farah was twenty-seven when she fled her war-torn homeland, crossing a river in a packed boat under a moonless sky. The vessel hit submerged debris and began taking on water; she remembers the slick, wet canvas of the life jacket pressing against her cheek, the passengers maintaining a desperate silence to avoid detection, and the crushing uncertainty of whether anyone would survive. She made it to the opposite bank, but the family she left behind did not. Twenty-eight years later, that texture still haunts her: as an HVAC technician, her fingers brush against insulation, damp concrete, and the rubber seals of pipes, and each time the physical sensation pulls her back into the memory-the overwhelm and shame of that night feel as immediate as ever.

The memory feels unreal, as if it happened to someone else, yet the emotion is paralyzing. When it surfaces-often triggered by standing water in a flooded basement or the sudden quiet when a mechanical system shuts off-she finds herself automatically surveying the room for exits, planning the quickest route to safety. This scanning, however, makes her acutely aware of every surface and sound. The texture of a damp paper towel, the coarse feel of ductwork, any resemblance to that life jacket now becomes a trigger in its own right, sending her mind reeling back to the boat. Her shame about surviving also makes her hypervigilant to the same texture, so that even a minor touch can reignite the memory. At the same time, the unusual silence she often encounters in empty mechanical rooms feels deeply threatening; she has come to believe that quiet means something dangerous is about to happen. That sense of threat itself summons a flashback-she is suddenly back on the water, hearing the hull creak-and the flashback in turn confirms that she must remain on guard.

She dwells intensely on what the smugglers and soldiers did to her family, a rumination that keeps the memory raw and magnifies her sense that danger is still present. The habit of checking her surroundings-scanning every corner, every exit-makes her perceive ordinary silences as ominous, heightening the constant sense of threat. And the act of vigilance also triggers memories of scanning the dark water for another boat, so that the very strategy she uses to feel safe reawakens the past. Over months, this cycle has cost her: she turned down a promotion that required working in an unfamiliar building because she could not bear the uncertainty of a new layout. Her world is shrinking. Recently, while repairing a boiler in a silent basement, a water pipe burst, and the rush of flooding triggered a full flashback that left her curled on the floor, unable to move. That was when she finally sought help. She is terrified of losing her job, but she also hopes that maybe she can learn to remember without being consumed.
